sections.title: Overview
sections.body_md:
This is a **long-only swing trading** system for US stocks and ETFs. It only buys shares with cash and sells shares it already holds. It never uses margin or leverage, never sells short, and never trades options.

Once a day, on weekdays at about 9:35 AM ET, it does five things:

1. Downloads daily price history.
2. Checks the overall market (SPY) to decide whether buying is allowed at all.
3. Scores and ranks a fixed list of 35 tickers.
4. Applies sizing and risk rules.
5. Places orders on an **Alpaca paper (simulated) account** and refreshes this page.

Every decision is a fixed rule. There is no manual approval step, and no AI forecast has any say in what gets bought (see the Kronos section). The same decision code is used for the backtest and the daily run, so the two cannot drift apart.

*This is a paper-trading experiment, not financial advice.*

sections.title: Data sources
sections.body_md:
- **yfinance (Yahoo Finance):** daily open, high, low, close and volume bars from 2012-01-01 onward, adjusted for splits and dividends. This is the only source of price data for signals. If the run happens before about 4:20 PM ET on a trading day, the unfinished current-day bar is dropped, so signals always use the last completed close.
- **Alpaca paper API (paper-api.alpaca.markets):** the broker. It supplies account equity, cash, last-close equity and current positions, and it receives the orders.
- **Kronos (Kronos-small model):** an AI price-forecasting model that produces a 10-day forecast for the top candidates and current holdings. It is shown on this page for information only and does not affect any trade.

No news, earnings, fundamentals, social media or options data are used. The system reads prices and volume only.

sections.title: The universe (35 tickers)
sections.body_md:
The system only ever considers this fixed list:

- **Broad market ETFs (4):** SPY, QQQ, VTI, IWM
- **Sector ETFs (11):** XLK, XLF, XLE, XLV, XLY, XLP, XLI, XLU, XLB, XLRE, XLC
- **Large-cap stocks (20):** AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, GOOGL, META, AVGO, TSLA, BRK-B, JPM, LLY, V, WMT, XOM, UNH, COST, NFLX, ORCL, HD, MA

SPY and VTI are treated as one correlated group, so the system never holds both at the same time.

sections.title: When it runs
sections.body_md:
- A scheduled job runs **every weekday at about 9:35 AM ET**, shortly after the market opens.
- Signals are calculated from the **previous day's close**. Orders are market orders (good for the day) that fill at or near the open.
- Sell orders go first, and the system waits up to 60 seconds for them to fill. Buys then use the cash that is available.
- The run is idempotent: it will not trade twice on the same date. After a real run, it refreshes the dashboard data and pushes it to this page.

sections.title: Step 1: the market regime filter
sections.body_md:
Before looking at any individual stock, the system checks SPY (the S&P 500 ETF) against its 50-day and 200-day simple moving averages (SMA). This sets one of three regimes:

- **Bull:** SPY closes above both its 50-day and its 200-day SMA. New buys are allowed. Existing positions are managed normally.
- **Caution:** SPY closes above its 200-day SMA but below its 50-day SMA. **No new buys.** Existing positions are held, and their stops stay active.
- **Bear:** SPY closes below its 200-day SMA. **Sell everything and stay in cash.** This check comes before the stop check, so every position is closed.

If there is not yet 200 days of SPY history, the regime is "warmup" and nothing is bought. The regime is shown on the dashboard along with the exact SPY values behind it.

sections.title: Step 2: which stocks qualify
sections.body_md:
A ticker must pass **all** of these tests on the latest close to be eligible:

- Close is above its 50-day SMA, and the 50-day SMA is above the 200-day SMA (a confirmed uptrend).
- RSI (14-day) is between **45 and 78**. This avoids both weak, falling names and overheated ones.
- 6-month momentum is **positive**.
- Average daily dollar volume (price times shares) over the last 20 days is above **$50 million**, so positions can be traded easily.

sections.title: Step 3: scoring and ranking
sections.body_md:
Eligible tickers are ranked by a score built from momentum, which is the tendency of recent winners to keep winning.

**Momentum measures** (both skip the most recent 5 trading days to avoid short-term reversals):
- 6-month momentum = close 5 days ago divided by close 126 days ago, minus 1.
- 3-month momentum = close 5 days ago divided by close 60 days ago, minus 1.

**Score** (higher is better, maximum 1.2):
- 0.6 times the percentile rank of 6-month momentum across the universe
- plus 0.4 times the percentile rank of 3-month momentum across the universe
- plus 0.1 if recent volume is picking up (20-day average volume above the 60-day average)
- plus 0.1 if the close is within 5% of its 52-week high

The highest scores are bought first. The system buys the top-ranked eligible names until it has 5 positions, skipping any name already held and skipping VTI if SPY is held (or the reverse). Kronos adds nothing to the score.

sections.title: Position sizing
sections.body_md:
Each new position is sized as the **smaller** of two limits:

- **Position cap:** 20% of account equity.
- **Risk rule:** 3% of account equity divided by the stop distance, where stop distance is 4.5 times the stock's 14-day ATR (average true range, a measure of daily volatility) as a percentage of price.

In practice, calmer stocks hit the 20% cap, and more volatile stocks get a smaller size so that a stop-out costs about 3% of the account. The 20% cap applies whenever the stop is within 15% of the price.

Other sizing rules:
- **Maximum 5 positions** at once.
- A **1% cash buffer** is always kept.
- If the cash left would fund less than 25% of the intended size, the buy is skipped.
- Orders are fractional-share dollar amounts, funded by cash only. Buying power from margin is never used.

sections.title: Exits
sections.body_md:
A position is sold when any one of these happens, checked in this order on the daily run:

1. **Bear regime:** SPY closes below its 200-day SMA, so every position is sold.
2. **ATR trailing stop:** the close is at or below *(highest close since entry minus 4.5 times the 14-day ATR)*. The reference high can only move up, so the stop trails a rising stock and is never pulled down by a pullback. It is checked at the close and executed at the next day's open.

Things the live system **does not** do:
- It does **not** sell on a close below the 50-day SMA (this option exists in the code but is switched off in the live settings).
- It does **not** sell just because a holding drops in the ranking (also switched off).
- It does **not** rebalance, trim or add to winners. A position runs until it is stopped out or the market turns bear, and then it is closed in full. Replacement buys happen only in a bull regime and only when a slot is free.

sections.title: Risk guards
sections.body_md:
- **Daily loss limit:** if account equity is down 3% or more versus the previous close, new entries are blocked on that run. The live check uses the equity and last-close equity figures reported by Alpaca. This stops new buying only; it does not force sales.
- **Paper-only lock:** the broker connection refuses to start unless the Alpaca URL is a paper one. Switching to a real-money account would require deliberately setting a separate override (`SWING_ALLOW_LIVE=1`) after the paper results are reviewed.
- **Long-only, cash-only:** orders are limited to buying with cash and selling shares already held. There is no shorting, margin or options code path.
- **Account blocked check:** if Alpaca reports the account is blocked, the run stops with an error rather than trading.
- **Position limits:** 5 positions, 20% each, one of SPY or VTI, and a 1% cash buffer, as described above.

sections.title: Kronos: display only
sections.body_md:
Kronos is an open-source AI model trained on price candlesticks. On each run, the system gives it recent daily bars (up to the last 400) for the 12 highest-ranked candidates plus anything currently held. It returns an expected 10-day return, using 4 sampled forecast paths averaged together. That number appears next to each pick on the dashboard.

**It has zero weight in every decision.** The code supports a Kronos weight in the score and an optional veto on forecasts below a set level, but both are switched off. The reason is a test of its track record:

- 208 forecasts across 13 dates, from 2024-10-01 to 2025-03-26, 10-day horizon, scored against what actually happened.
- The rank correlation between forecast and actual return was **0.04** (statistic t = 0.41), which is statistically indistinguishable from zero. A useful signal would be meaningfully higher.
- The forecast called the direction right **48.6%** of the time, versus a base rate of **51.0%** for stocks rising over a 10-day window, so no better than guessing.
- The top quartile of forecasts averaged a +0.03% real 10-day return, versus -0.37% for the bottom quartile. That is directionally right but tiny and not statistically reliable on this sample.
- Only 31% of the 13 test dates had a positive correlation.

The test sample is small, so Kronos is not proven useless, but there is no evidence of an edge today. It stays on the page as an interesting data point while the evidence builds.

sections.title: Backtest results
sections.body_md:
The system was tested on daily data from **2016-01-04 to 2026-10-30** (about 10.8 years), starting with a hypothetical $5,000. Signals used each day's close, and trades filled at the next day's open with 5 basis points (0.05%) of assumed slippage per side. Fractional shares and no leverage. The rule settings were chosen by a **walk-forward** process: each year, the best of 12 setting combinations over prior history was used for that year. The same setting won every year (3% risk per trade, 4.5 times ATR stop, no 50-day exit), and it is the one used live.

**Strategy versus buying and holding SPY:**
- Total return: **+514.8%** versus +347.0%
- Compound annual growth rate (CAGR): **18.3%** versus 14.8%
- Maximum drawdown (worst peak-to-trough fall): **-25.7%** versus -33.7%
- Sharpe ratio (return per unit of volatility): **1.05** versus 0.87
- Average exposure to the market: 75.9% of the time invested

**Trade statistics:** 174 trades. Win rate **50.6%**, average win +18.5%, average loss -5.3%, average trade +6.7%, profit factor 3.54, average holding about 63 trading days. Exits: 119 ATR stops and 55 bear-regime exits.

**Calendar-year returns (strategy versus SPY):**
- 2016: +43.9% vs +13.6%
- 2017: +24.0% vs +21.7%
- 2018: +21.2% vs -4.6%
- 2019: +16.7% vs +31.2%
- 2020: +53.9% vs +18.3%
- 2021: +11.4% vs +28.7%
- 2022: -7.6% vs -18.2%
- 2023: +29.8% vs +26.2%
- 2024: +42.5% vs +24.9%
- 2025: **-8.1%** vs +17.7%
- 2026 (through Oct 30): **-9.5%** vs +11.7%

**Sensitivity to trading costs:** with 10 bps of slippage per side, CAGR is 17.9% and Sharpe 1.03. With 25 bps, CAGR is 16.8% and Sharpe 0.98.

sections.title: Honest caveats
sections.body_md:
Please read the backtest numbers with these limits in mind:

- **Survivorship and hindsight bias.** The 20 individual stocks are today's well-known large caps (NVDA, AVGO, META and so on), picked knowing they went on to be successful. A real 2016 version of this list would have looked different. The stock picking adds a lot of the return: a version limited to ETFs only returned **6.6% CAGR** (Sharpe 0.69, max drawdown -14.0%) against 14.8% for SPY. NVDA alone had 13 trades averaging +28.6%.
- **Recent losses.** The strategy lost money in **2025 (-8.1%)** and **2026 so far (-9.5%)** while SPY rose, so the most recent period is the weakest. A momentum system that waits for confirmed uptrends can be late and get shaken out by sharp reversals.
- **Few big winners.** The win rate is only about 50%. The results depend on winners averaging +18.5% against losers of -5.3%, so a stretch without big winners can look poor for a long time.
- **Settings were tuned on past data.** Walk-forward testing helps, but the grid was small, and the live settings are also the best in-sample over the full history. Real-world results are likely to be lower than the backtest.
- **A simple alternative is competitive on risk.** Holding SPY only when it is above its 200-day average returned 10.7% CAGR with a -19.5% drawdown and a 0.92 Sharpe. The swing strategy has a better Sharpe (1.05), but also a deeper drawdown.
- **Real fills differ.** The backtest fills at the open with fixed slippage. Paper orders are market orders placed at about 9:35 AM, and the opening minutes can be noisy.
- **Holding period.** The average hold in the test was about 63 trading days, closer to a few months than a few days or weeks, because positions are held until stopped out.
- **The account is paper money.** There is no real capital at risk, and the system has only a short live record so far. Past results do not predict future ones.
